messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: using subset of data from global detection function in MRDS
parts:
Nicole:

We placed checks inside the DSM package to ensure that all detected
objects used in the DSM analysis had associated detection probabilities
from previous fittings of ddf() that resides in the MRDS package. We
did that by checking that the same filter was used both for fitting the
detection function and fitting the density surface. I suspect that is
the check of which you are running afoul when trying to use the global
detection function to apply to sightings only from the northern study area.

One way to accomplish what you wish, is to do a little 'mining' inside
the R workspace created by Distance. Fit a global detection function to
all of your data using ddf(). Having done so, you will have a object
called ddf.x (where x is a number corresponding to the analysis you have
run). You can then examine the contents of that object in which you
will be able to find a detection probability estimated for all detected
objects in your survey. You may access these detection probabilities
for the northern region, and insert the detection probabilities into a
Distance project that contains the survey information associated with
the northern region.

Notice the Model Definition Properties window associated with the DSM
engine where you specify the density surface model you wish to fit.
Look at the top right portion of the window, you will see a section for
'Detection probabilities.' Most commonly, you select the fitted
function that you used to estimate the detection function. However, you
may also choose 'table of values' in which case you are asked to choose
a field from the observation layer that contains the detection
probability associated with the detected objects.

It is through that mechanism that you can specify detection
probabilities for your northern region that you have derived from
fitting a detection function to all of your observations throughout your
study area.

If you have questions about those steps, contact me off line for further
clarification.
